groups.title: Quality
groups.intro: AI does the repetitive hours. People check the result.

faq.a: No. AI takes over the repetitive hours, and a person still reviews every piece of work before it reaches you.
A person on our team reviews every piece of work before it reaches you: code, designs, writing and automations. AI drafts and tests. People decide what ships.

faq.q: Why is your team in the Philippines?
faq.a: Because the skills are there. The Philippines’ IT and business services industry earned US$40.3 billion in 2025 and employs 1.89 million people¹, and its English proficiency is rated “High”, second in Asia². Our costs are lower there, and we pass the difference on to you.

faq.q: How do we know it’s working?
faq.a: Before we start, we agree what success looks like, using your own numbers, like hours saved or more sales. Then you see progress every week, in writing.
You hear it from us early, with a plan to fix it. When something goes wrong, we say “we”, and we fix it.

sources.text: IBPAP (IT and Business Process Association of the Philippines), industry revenue and employment, 2025. Retrieved 2026-11-02.
EF English Proficiency Index 2025, Philippines. Retrieved 2026-11-02.

groups.title: Price
groups.intro: Published starting prices, a fixed quote and nothing on the invoice you didn’t expect.

faq.a: Every core service has a published starting price: websites from [PRICE], the AI check-up from [PRICE], AI automation projects from [PRICE] and embedded developers from [PRICE] a month. Before work starts, you get a fixed quote that lists everything we’ll charge.

Two reasons. AI does the repetitive work, so a project needs fewer billable hours. And our team is based in the Philippines, where our costs are lower than in the US, the UK or Australia. We pass the difference on to you.
No. Changes are quoted before we do them. There are no per-seat fees on the tools we build, and AI usage, like model fees, is passed on at cost and shown on your invoice.

faq.q: Can we cancel a monthly plan?
faq.a: Yes, with [30] days’ notice. You own what we build, so it stays with you.

faq.q: What if a cheaper tool would do the job?
faq.a: We’ll tell you. If an off-the-shelf tool or a simpler fix costs you less, we say so, even when it means less work for us.

groups.title: Time zones
groups.intro: Our team is in the Philippines. Here’s how our day lines up with yours.

faq.a: In the Philippines. Sydney is two hours ahead of us, or three during Australian daylight saving. For US partners, we work while you sleep: brief us before you log off, and you’ll see progress when you log on. For UK partners, our afternoon is your morning.
We agree a regular time for calls when we start. Your evening in the US is our morning, your morning in the UK is our afternoon, and in Australia most of the working day overlaps.

faq.q: What happens when the clocks change?
faq.a: We follow them. The Philippines doesn’t change its clocks, so when Sydney, the US or the UK move theirs, we move our call times to match.

sources.text: NSW Government, Daylight saving (Sydney is UTC+10, or UTC+11 in daylight saving). Retrieved 2026-11-02.
NIST, Local time FAQs (US time zones and daylight saving). Retrieved 2026-11-02.

groups.title: Data and security
groups.intro: Your data stays where you decide.

faq.a: It stays where you decide. We work inside your systems wherever we can, take only the access a job needs, and never use your data to train anything you don’t own.

You see progress every week, a person reviews every piece of work, and your data stays in your systems wherever possible. The Philippines also has a national privacy law, the Data Privacy Act of 2012, enforced by an independent National Privacy Commission⁵.
Only the people on your project, with only the access the job needs. It’s your system, so you can see and remove our access at any time.

faq.q: Do you work with regulated industries?
faq.a: Yes. Projects in healthcare, finance, insurance and legal start with a privacy and compliance review, because those industries have stricter rules about data.

sources.text: Republic Act No. 10173, Data Privacy Act of 2012. Supreme Court E-Library. Retrieved 2026-11-02.

groups.title: Working together
groups.intro: We work as part of your team, and we stay after launch.

faq.a: With an AI check-up, a short first project. In [two weeks], we learn how your business runs, find where AI could save you time or money, and give you a written plan with a fixed quote for the first fix. It costs from [PRICE].
Understand, Plan, Build, and Run and grow. We learn how your business works and where it gets stuck, pick the right fix, build it, then keep it running and help you win more customers.

faq.q: Will you tell us if AI isn’t the answer?
faq.a: Yes. The right fix might be better design, extra developers or a simpler tool. If AI isn’t the right answer, we say so, even when it means less work for us.
Yes. Where most agencies hand over the project and move on, we stay to keep everything running, improve it over time and help you win more customers.
You do, including the code and the documentation. Work happens in your accounts and tools wherever possible.
